pages.title: Three open seminars
pages.content:
THE SEMINARS

Next: Thu 21 January 2027

Three open seminars

Minori Seminars opens three distinct one-day management programmes to the public at our seminar room in Rotterdam. Each programme is designed around a specific leadership transition and held on select Thursdays.

New to leading a team

First-Time Manager Day

Built for managers in their first two years with 3 to 12 people: the first conversations and practical delegation.

Thursdays · Marit Coenen

Leading a department through change

Leading Through Change

For heads of department steering a reorganisation, a merger or a new system, with colleagues who face the same.

Thursdays · Samuel Adeyemi

Running the firm

The Owner's Day

For owners and managing directors of firms with 10 to 80 staff who want to step back from daily operations.

Thursdays · Claire Dubois

PROGRAMMES

The three programmes

We host three focused seminars throughout the spring term. First-Time Manager Day is built for professionals in their first two years of leading a team of three to twelve people. Leading Through Change supports heads of department steering teams through reorganisations, system migrations, or organisational mergers.

The Owner's Day is dedicated to managing directors and founders of companies with ten to eighty staff who need to transition from direct supervision to sustainable delegation. Every seminar gathers sixteen participants around four tables of four, creating an environment focused on peer dialogue, practical frameworks, and real operational decisions rather than passive lectures.

SHARED

What all three share

While each seminar addresses a different stage of management, all three share an identical structure and standard of care. Every seminar runs on a Thursday from 09:30 to 17:00, with doors opening at 09:00 for coffee.

Seats are capped strictly at sixteen to ensure focused conversation, led by one facilitator and one co-facilitator. The open seminar fee of €640 per seat includes a shared seated lunch, continuous refreshments, and a comprehensive printed workbook of seminar notes to take back to your desk.

Organisations sending a leadership cohort can reserve an entire table of four for €2,240.

See the hour-by-hour plan on how the day runs, or check the six dates and fees.

pages.title: First-Time Manager Day
pages.content:
THE SEMINARS

Next: Thu 21 January 2027

First-Time Manager Day

A one-day seminar for professionals in their first two years of leading a team, focusing on the essential shift from individual contribution to managing others. Held at our seminar room in Rotterdam on Thursdays.

€640

per seat, excl. VAT

€2,240

table of four

THE DAY

Who the day is for and the morning idea

This seminar is designed specifically for people managing three to twelve team members who have stepped into leadership within the last twenty-four months. The morning session begins at the flipchart exploring one central insight: the first conversation is the job.

Most new managers struggle because they attempt to complete operational tasks themselves while treating team interactions as interruptions. Facilitated by Marit Coenen, the morning establishes how clear expectations, structured listening, and deliberate communication form the foundation of managerial effectiveness, giving new leaders the perspective needed to step back from technical execution.

HOURS

09:30

Opening at the tables

Doors open at 09:00 for coffee. At half past nine we begin at the tables with introductions in fours, building shared ground and working trust between peers.

10:00

Morning session at the flipchart

The facilitator draws out the one idea of the day on the flipchart, then unpacks it with practical examples and discussion at every table.

12:30

Lunch at the same tables

A seated lunch is served in the room, with shared food and unhurried conversation. Dietary needs are met when you tell us at enrolment.

13:30

Case clinic

You bring one current situation you lead through and work it in pairs, testing the options you really have with a colleague who sits across from you.

15:45

Your next conversation

You write down the conversation you will have next, read it to your table and refine it into clear steps. We close promptly at 17:00.

CASE CLINIC

The case clinic and takeaway materials

During the afternoon, participants work in pairs on real supervisory challenges brought from their own workplaces. You will draft the exact structure and language for an upcoming conversation with a team member, whether addressing missed deadlines or clarifying ambiguous responsibilities, and present it to your table of four for critique. The day concludes at 17:00 with your printed seminar notes workbook in hand.

An individual seat is €640 and a table of four is €2,240 excluding Dutch VAT. Spring term dates are Thursday 21 January 2027 and Thursday 11 March 2027.

DATES

Dates, facilitator and price

Spring term 2027: Thu 21 January 2027 and Thu 11 March 2027, 09:30 to 17:00, doors 09:00. Led by Marit Coenen. Brakel Print & Pack sent two new team leads to this day. Read it on our stories page, or see every date and fee.

The seminar timetable

Our seven-hour schedule divides the day into four structured conversations. Doors open at 09:00, allowing participants to arrive and enjoy coffee before the 09:30 opening at the tables, where introductions take place in groups of four. At 10:00, the facilitator leads the morning session at the flipchart, unpacking the core conceptual framework of the day.

A shared lunch is served at 12:30 at the same tables. At 13:30, the case clinic begins, where you examine your workplace situation in pairs. At 15:45, you draft your next critical conversation and present it to your table, closing promptly at 17:00.

pages.title: The facilitators
pages.content:
THE FACILITATORS

Next: Thu 21 January 2027

The facilitators

Our seminars are led by seasoned practitioners who facilitate structured workplace reflection rather than delivering generic classroom lectures. Every session is staffed by one lead facilitator and one co-facilitator.

PEOPLE

Marit Coenen

Founder and lead facilitator

Opens First-Time Manager Day at the flipchart and has led the seminar room since our first open day.

Samuel Adeyemi

Facilitator, Leading Through Change

Works with heads of department on honest communication through a merger, a reorganisation or a new system.

Claire Dubois

Facilitator, The Owner's Day

Helps owners and managing directors delegate real authority without losing governance or accountability.

Tobias Brandt

Co-facilitator, case clinics

Supports the pair clinics at the tables and delivers our in-house programmes in German.

Wen-Yu Lin

Co-facilitator

Co-facilitates seminar days and leads in-house training in Mandarin and English.

Inès Laurent

Enrolment and participant care

Answers every seat request at the booking desk and confirms your place within two working days.

Joost van Dam

Seminar room and operations

Looks after the room, the catering and the facilities on the fourth floor of Lindehuis.

HOW WE WORK

How our facilitation works

At Minori Seminars, we believe effective management training requires structured inquiry rather than academic monologues. Our facilitators do not rely on pre-packaged slide presentations or scripted corporate formulas.

Instead, they stand at the flipchart to map out the real operational dynamics occurring inside your business, challenging assumptions and clarifying communication patterns. By pairing a lead facilitator with an experienced co-facilitator in every seminar room, we ensure that every table of four receives dedicated attention during pair clinics and individual writing exercises, ensuring every concept translates into concrete workplace behaviour.

THE TEAM

The Minori seminar team

Our team consists of seven dedicated professionals. Marit Coenen is our founder and lead facilitator for First-Time Manager Day. Samuel Adeyemi facilitates Leading Through Change, while Claire Dubois leads The Owner's Day. Tobias Brandt co-facilitates our case clinics and delivers in-house programmes in German.

Wen-Yu Lin co-facilitates sessions and leads corporate training in Mandarin and English. Inès Laurent manages participant care and enrolment at our booking desk, answering all seat requests. Joost van Dam oversees seminar room operations, catering logistics, and facilities on the fourth floor of Lindehuis.

pages.content:
ABOUT

Next: Thu 21 January 2027

About Minori

Founded in 2011, Minori Seminars provides focused, practical management training for mid-sized organisations from our dedicated fourth-floor seminar room in Rotterdam.

Minori Seminars was established in 2011 as the internal management-training desk for a consortium of mid-sized commercial enterprises. Having identified a persistent lack of practical, distraction-free leadership education, we opened three of our established seminar days to the public in 2016.

We deliberately offer only three seminar programmes and host sessions exclusively on Thursdays. This focused schedule ensures our facilitators remain active practitioners in commercial management throughout the rest of the week, bringing fresh, unvarnished insight into the seminar room rather than repeating outdated academic business theory.

THE ROOM

The seminar room and visiting details

Our offices and seminar room are situated on the 4th floor of Lindehuis, located at Kade 41, 3024 AB Rotterdam, Netherlands. The room is configured with four oak tables of four, surrounded by wide windows that provide calm natural daylight. The venue is located approximately ten minutes on foot from Rotterdam Centraal station.

Doors open at 09:00 on seminar Thursdays, and sessions run from 09:30 until 17:00. General administrative inquiries and seat reservations are handled by email at seats@minori-seminars.example during office hours, Monday through Friday, 09:00 to 17:30 CET.

When you contact seats@minori-seminars.example, we collect only the necessary details required to administer your seat reservation or in-house booking. Who do I contact about my data?

Seat reservations may be cancelled free of charge up to fourteen days before the scheduled seminar date. Invoices are issued via email within two working days of your reservation request and are payable under thirty-day commercial terms. posts.title: The First Conversation Is the Job: Making the Shift to Management
posts.excerpt: Why new managers must step back from individual technical tasks and recognize that structured conversations with their team are the true foundation of leadership.
posts.content:
When a specialist is promoted to manage a team, the initial instinct is almost always to work faster. Most new team leads believe their promotion was an endorsement of their technical output, so they attempt to maintain their previous individual workload while answering queries from colleagues in the margins of the day. Within three months, this approach leads to exhaustion, missed deadlines, and growing friction across the department. At Minori Seminars, where we have observed this transition since our founding in 2011, we address this tension directly in our First-Time Manager Day. The fundamental shift in management is not working harder at technical tasks; it is recognizing that conversation itself has become your primary work.

On Thursday mornings in our seminar room on the fourth floor of Lindehuis in Rotterdam, lead facilitator Marit Coenen opens the session at the flipchart with sixteen participants gathered around four tables of four. The core morning idea is straightforward yet demanding: the first conversation is the job. When a team member struggles with deadlines or produces ambiguous work, inexperienced managers tend to re-do the assignment themselves late in the evening. They treat discussing the issue as an unwelcome interruption to real work. In reality, sitting down with that colleague to establish clear expectations, inspect assumptions, and agree on next steps is the actual core of supervisory responsibility.

This transition became evident when Brakel Print & Pack, a regional packaging company of forty-two staff, sent two newly appointed shift supervisors to our seminar room. Both supervisors were exceptional craftspeople who had spent years operating equipment alongside the very colleagues they were now expected to guide. Their central anxiety was how to address slipping standards without damaging peer relationships. During the morning discussions, they realized that silence or indirect hints only created confusion. Clear, calm, and structured communication was not an act of hostility; it was the fairest way to lead former peers.

During the afternoon case clinic, participants move from theory into structured practice. Working in pairs, each manager examines a live situation from their workplace and drafts the specific sentences required for their next conversation. At Brakel Print & Pack, the two leads scripted how they would address upcoming performance reviews and shift handovers, reading their drafts aloud to their table for immediate critique. By the time the session closed at 17:00, both had tested their phrasing and refined their approach in a quiet room away from factory pressures.

Stepping away from the desk for a single Thursday provides the perspective needed to stop reacting to urgent operational noise. When managers understand how to conduct deliberate, focused conversations, they no longer need to carry the entire department's workload on their own shoulders. By focusing on structured listening and unambiguous agreements, new leaders build the trust and autonomy their teams need to succeed.
